Early Reception into the NT Canon
Early Reception into the NT Canon
It must be stated that some in the early church doubted Petrine
authorship. R. Bauckham writes, “Evidently 2 Peter was known
throughout the second century, at least in some circles, but not widely
used.”
He states that the churches that had the letter may have known
that Peter did not write it and consequently viewed it as being in the
same category as the rest of the pseudo
Petrine works.
This could
explain the lack of widespread circulation.
Bauckham concludes by
stating that the letter was gradually accepted, and Jerome’s firm stamp
of approval probably helped its case.
Thus its attestation in the early
church is clearly weak.
Kruger, as stated above, notes those who acknowledge its
canonicity: Origen (c. AD 254; who used it, calling it Scripture, though
he had some doubts about its authorship), Athanasius (c. AD 373),
Gregory of Nazianzus (c. AD 390), Jerome (c. AD 420), and Au
gustine
